 177: ## [2026-09-20] Q2-Submission Hardening — 8 Critical Fixes (COMPLETED, results regenerated)
 178: 
 179: ### Q2-1 `src/train.py` — BiC stage-local correction bug fix
 180: - **Fixed:** `BiasCorrector.apply()` now only corrects `n_old:n_old+n_new` (previously corrected all future classes).
 181: - **Fixed:** `fit_stage()` now stores `n_new` per stage; stage dict = `{"n_old", "n_new", "alpha", "beta"}`.
 182: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.3 — baseline with incorrect implementation is unpublishable. All BiC results regenerated.
 183: 
 184: ### Q2-2 `experiments/run_hparam_sweep.py` / `src/train.py` — Train/Val/Test methodology
 185: - Sweep now uses `val_frac=0.10` on STIN; hyperparameters selected on **validation ACC_val - FM_val**, never test.
 186: - `train_continual()` returns validation matrix `V` alongside test matrix `R`.
 187: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.1 — test-set leakage invalidates main comparison if uncorrected.
 188: 
 189: ### Q2-3 `experiments/run_validation_tune.py` (NEW) — Per-method/arch validation tuning
 190: - 7 methods × 3 architectures tuned on CuCD-ID validation (3 seeds each), small grids per method family.
 191: - Winners frozen to `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json` → used by ALL subsequent experiments.
 192: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.2 — single sweep on MLP/STIN does not transfer to GRU/CNN (confirmed by ablation).
 193: 
 194: ### Q2-4 `src/data_utils.py` / `experiments/run_purged_temporal.py` (NEW) — Purged temporal protocol
 195: - Added `build_cucd_id_tasks_purged_temporal()` with 22s-equivalent (0.02 rad) purge gaps on `TimeRadians`.
 196: - Layout: `[Train | Purge | Val | Purge | Test]` — exceeds 20s sliding-window horizon + 20-22s clearing pauses.
 197: - STIN keeps existing `id`-based temporal (no purge — secondary stress test only).
 198: - Dual-protocol evaluation: **IID (benchmark)** + **Forward Temporal + Purge (stress test)**.
 199: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.6/0.7 — IID numbers (~0.92) vs temporal (~0.20) gap must be explicit, not hidden.
 200: 
 201: ### Q2-5 `src/metrics.py` / `src/train.py` / `experiments/run_main.py` — Dual memory + compute accounting
 202: - **Persistent footprint:** INT8 weights + INT8 replay + FP16 EWC (deployed storage).
 203: - **Peak training RAM:** FP32 weights + gradients + Adam(2×params) + activations + batch + replay_batch + teacher + temp.
 204: - **MAC/update:** MAC/sample × N_train_samples × epochs (not just MAC/forward).
 205: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.14/15/18 — Q2 systems reviewer will demand complete resource accounting.
 206: 
 207: ### Q2-6 `experiments/config.py` / `experiments/run_main.py` / `experiments/run_fewshot.py` — Final consistent rerun
 208: - **Main matrix:** 10 seeds (540 runs: 2 datasets × 3 archs × 9 methods × 10 seeds) with frozen per-method/arch hparams.
 209: - **Few-shot:** 5 seeds, inherits frozen hparams, only K varies (K=5..300), uplink Pareto outputs.
 210: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.4/9/10 — central comparison must be internally consistent and statistically defensible.
 211: 
 212: ### Q2-7 `src/metrics.py` / `experiments/run_stats.py` / `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py` — Journal-grade metrics + stats
 213: - **Primary metrics:** Macro-F1, Balanced Accuracy, BWT/FM (Accuracy supplementary).
 214: - **Per-class:** Final F1 + forgetting for each attack class (CuCD-ID).
 215: - **Stats:** Exact paired permutation test (SciPy if available, else NumPy) + Holm correction + Cohen's d + 95% CI.
 216: - Headline comparisons only (no elaborate stats for every ablation).
 217: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.10/11/23/24 — "p=0.043 proves superiority" is not Q2-citable.
 218: 
 219: ### Q2-8 `experiments/run_feature_order.py` (NEW) — Architecture interpretation fix
 220: - 4 feature permutations × MLP/GRU/CNN × 4 methods × 2 seeds.
 221: - MLP stable; GRU/CNN sensitive → confirms MLP as primary tabular backbone, GRU/CNN as stress tests.
 222: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.21/22 — GRU/CNN on reshaped tabular features are not genuine temporal models.
 223: 
 224: ### Q2-9 New tooling for reproducibility
 225: - `experiments/check_consistency.py` — Verifies main vs few-shot hyperparameter consistency, seed counts, config provenance.
 226: - `experiments/create_manifest.py` — Creates `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` with full provenance (git commit, env, datasets, protocols, frozen hparams, outputs).
 227: - `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` — Complete machine-readable reproducibility record.
 228: 
 229: ### Pipeline integration
 230: - `run_all.py`: CORE (gradient → sweep → validation_tune → main) → PHASE2 (purged_temporal → fewshot → feature_order → ablations → per_class → stats → robustness) → REPORT (plots → summary).
 231: - `analysis/plots.py`: CI bars, Pareto figures, dual-protocol comparison, updated column names for persistent/peak memory.
 232: - `experiments/generate_summary_report.py`: Journal tables (Macro-F1 primary), dual memory, uplink Pareto.

 288: ## [Unreleased] Phase 0 — MUST-FIX protocol corrections (no results invalidated, old API kept)
 289: 
 290: ### 0.1 `src/data_utils.py` — train/val/test + temporal (leakage-safe) splits
 291: - **Added:** `Task.X_val / y_val` (optional, default `None`), `TaskSequence.split_mode`, `val_frac` plumbing.
 292: - **Added:** `_stratified_train_val_test_split()` — test is locked before any train/val sampling; val is carved from train pool only.
 293: - **Added:** `build_cucd_id_tasks_temporal()` / `build_stin_tasks_temporal()` — per-class **block (time-ordered) split** instead of row-shuffle, because CuCD-ID features contain `SlidingWindow* / MessageCountInWindow / MessageRateInWindow` computed over neighbouring rows; random row-shuffle leaks correlated windows between train and test and inflates absolute ACC. Old builders kept byte-identical behaviour when `val_frac=0.0` and `split_mode="random"`.
 294: - **Why:** reviewer P0.1 (sliding-window leakage) + P0.2 (no val/test separation). Relative rankings (replay >> finetune) survive leakage, but absolute numbers (e.g. MLP 0.93 / permuted-order 0.995) are not Q1/Q2-credible without this.
 295: 
 296: ### 0.2 `src/train.py` — true joint-from-scratch + bias-correction hook + balanced replay option
 297: - **Added:** `method="joint_scratch"` — re-initialises the model and trains on the union of all training data seen so far at each task boundary. Old `method="joint"` is kept but renamed in docs as `cumulative warm-start` (it continues from current weights, `train.py` pool logic). New method is the strict upper bound.
 298: - **Added:** `BiasCorrector` (BiC-style, 2 params per task-group: `logits_new -> alpha*logits_new + beta`, fit on held-out val/buffer, trunk+head frozen). Phase 0 exposes `fit_bic()` / `apply()` + `bias_correction` flag plumbing; full BiC training loop lands in Phase 1.
 299: - **Added:** `replay_balance="uniform"|"class_balanced"` — reservoir sampling over-represents the large T0 class pool; balanced interleaving is the known fix for new-class head bias. Default stays `uniform` so old numbers reproduce.
 300: - **Why:** reviewer P0.3 (joint bound mislabelled) + P4 (bias is the dominant CIL failure; EWC `lambda=0` already best on GRU/CNN in `ablation_ewc_lambda.csv`, so regularisation alone cannot fix logit competition).
 301: 
 302: ### 0.3 `src/cmmu.py` — herding selector + val-balanced Fisher guidance

 366: ### 1.1 `src/train.py` — `lwf / bic / icarl` (all NumPy, CuCD-ID-first design)
 367: - **Added:** `_distill_dlogits` (Hinton KD gradient, T²-scaled, old-head columns only) + `_snapshot_teacher` (frozen trunk+old head before each growth step) + `_rebuild_herding_buffer` (equal exemplars/class, input-space herding — documented lite limitation vs embedding-space iCaRL).
 368: - `lwf`: memory-free distillation, no replay. `bic`: herding + balanced replay + distillation + full `(alpha,beta)` BiC grid fit on held-out val. `icarl` (lite): herding + balanced replay + distillation, softmax eval (NCM omitted — documented).
 369: - **Bug fixed during smoke test:** KD was first combined as convex `(1-lam)*CE + KD`, which at the default `distill_lambda=1.0` zeroed new-class learning (`lwf ACC~=chance`). Changed to additive `CE + lam*KD`; post-fix 3-epoch smoke (MLP/CuCD-ID): `bic 0.612 > full 0.415 ≈ replay 0.413 > icarl 0.326 > lwf 0.291`.
 370: - **Why:** reviewer P1.5 + base paper (BiC best, LwF/iCaRL family expected); tests stay on CuCD-ID first, STIN second — no generic dataset added per user constraint.
 371: 
 372: ### 1.2 `src/metrics.py` — detection + from-scratch stats
 373: - **Added:** `detection_scores_from_logits` (`1-p(normal)`), `_binary_auroc` (tie-averaged ranks), `_binary_aupr` (average precision), `_fpr_at_tpr`, `compute_detection_metrics` (AUROC/AUPR/FPR95+prevalence). STIN must not use these (no benign) — `run_main.final_detection_metrics` returns NaN there.
 374: - **Added:** `wilcoxon_signed_rank` (normal approx with tie correction, no scipy) for matched-seed method pairs.
 375: - Smoke finding (3 epochs, unconverged): detection AUROC stays ~1.0 even when ACC collapses (collapsed head predicts everything as attack) while FPR95 separates (`replay 0.001` vs `lwf 0.738`) — confirms classification-vs-detection dissociation is a paper-worthy RQ, matching the base paper's take-home.
 376: - **Why:** IDS paper without normal-vs-attack evaluation is rejectable; stats required for Q1/Q2 (5 seeds → min two-sided p=0.0625, so effects reported alongside p).
 377: 
 378: ### 1.3 `experiments/config.py` — broader matrix, more seeds
 379: - `METHODS` 5 → 9 (`+ lwf/bic/icarl/joint_scratch`, `joint` kept as legacy warm-start), `SEEDS` 3 → 5 (`[0..4]`). Matrix 90 → 270 runs.
 380: - **Why:** baseline breadth + variance credibility; `joint_scratch` is the citable upper bound.

 108: ## 2026-09-18 — Phase 2d temporal-vs-random (`results/temporal_compare.csv`, 40 runs: MLP × replay,icarl,bic,scratch × random|temporal × 5 seeds)
 109: - Random→temporal collapse for ALL methods incl. offline scratch: replay 0.923→0.202, icarl 0.967→0.288, bic 0.904→0.271, scratch 0.997→0.140. Diagnostic (scratch/temporal/seed0): train resubstitution 1.000 vs test 0.155; T0 self-accuracy 0.856→0.396 across tasks; new-task test ≈0. Cause: within-class mission-time drift — each attack occupies its own TimeRadians phase (e.g. storage_exhaustion spans 0.001–6.28 with MemoryAnonMB 19→74 early-vs-late); early-train vs late-test = attack-intensity extrapolation, and the T0-frozen scaler mismatches. So temporal-blocks ≠ leakage-free i.i.d. eval.
 110: - Paper position: headline stays random-split (i.i.d. within-scenario) WITH explicit sliding-window-leakage limitation; temporal reported as forward-extrapolation stress bound (truth between the two). A true group/scenario split needs scenario IDs the CSV lacks — flagged as data-collection future work, not fixable by splitting alone.
 111: - CNN is optimization-starved at frozen hparams: replay 0.484 (lr .003/25) → 0.718 (lr .01/50); icarl 0.463 → 0.856; scratch 0.841 → 0.961 (lr .01/50). Residual CL gap at best tune ≈ 0.10 (scratch 0.961 vs icarl 0.856). Conclusion: per-arch tune mandatory before any "CNN fails at CIL" claim; CNN viable but 2× epoch cost. Paper must report tuned CNN (lr=0.01/50ep) alongside frozen-hparam numbers, never silently swap.
 112: - Flag (a) from Phase-1 rerun resolved as optimization, not CL failure.

 114: ## 2026-09-18 — Phase 2b few-shot uplink (`results/fewshot.csv`, 182 runs: CuCD-ID, T0=700 fixed, K{5,10,25,50,100,150,300}, val_frac 0.10)
 115: - MLP mean ACC: icarl K=5: 0.732 (vs replay 0.509, bic 0.682) → K=50: 0.902 → K=150: 0.967 (reproduces matrix) → K=300: 0.990. Knee at K≈50 for MLP/icarl; replay/full need K≥100–150 to match. GRU needs K≥150 (icarl 0.736, replay 0.571) and only converges at K=300 (0.807/0.864). Uplink KB per K in `uplink_KB_total` column for the Pareto plot.
 116: - RQ4 answer draft: minimum viable uplink ≈ 50 samples/class for MLP+iCaRL, ≥150 for GRU; 5-shot works only with herding+distill+BiC (icarl/bic), never plain replay.
 117: - K=150 column consistency-checks the Phase-1 matrix (MLP replay 0.923, icarl 0.967, bic 0.904 — match).
 118: - Protocol: random split + `val_frac=0.10`, frozen STIN/MLP/full hparams (`lr=0.003, lambda=100, buf=256, frac=0.9`), 5 seeds, 9 methods. Ablations also rerun at 5 seeds (buffer 180 rows, lambda 210 rows); per-class + stats + figures + `RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` regenerated.
 119: - CuCD-ID ACC: MLP `icarl 0.967 > replay 0.923 ≈ full 0.921 > bic 0.904 >> collapse 0.250` (icarl-vs-replay p=0.345 n.s.; full-vs-replay p=0.50 n.s.); GRU `icarl 0.759 > replay 0.633 ≈ full 0.610 ≈ bic 0.604` (icarl-vs-replay p=0.043); CNN `bic 0.597 > replay 0.484 ≈ icarl 0.482 > full 0.404` (bic-vs-all p=0.043; icarl-vs-replay p=0.89 n.s.). Bounds: `joint_scratch` tops on MLP (0.997) / GRU (0.984) but **loses to warm `joint` on CNN** (0.858 vs 0.898) — CNN optimization flag.
 120: - STIN ACC: MLP `joint 0.661 ≈ scratch 0.657 ≈ bic 0.655 ≈ icarl 0.651 ≈ full 0.648 > replay 0.622` (bic-vs-joint p=0.89 n.s. — at ceiling); GRU `joint 0.664 > replay 0.571 ≈ scratch 0.576 > icarl 0.523`; CNN `joint 0.535 ≈ icarl 0.524 (p=0.69 n.s.) > replay 0.500 ≈ bic 0.495`, scratch collapses to 0.395 — same CNN-from-scratch flag, stronger.

FILE: ./PROJECT_CONTEXT.md
================================================================================
   1: # PROJECT_CONTEXT.md
   2: ### Class-Incremental Continual Learning for TinyML-Based Intrusion Detection in CubeSats
   3: 
   4: This document describes what the project is and what has been implemented in the codebase. It intentionally excludes performance results, accuracy numbers, or outcome data — it is a reference for the problem, design, and implementation only.
   5: 
   6: ---
   7: 
   8: ## 1. One-paragraph summary
   9: 
  10: A from-scratch (pure NumPy, no PyTorch/TensorFlow/autograd) implementation of **class-incremental continual learning** for onboard, memory-constrained intrusion detection on CubeSats. The **MLP is the primary backbone** — it directly processes the tabular telemetry feature vector. A compact GRU and 1-D CNN are evaluated as **architectural stress tests**, not genuine temporal sequence models. Nine continual-learning configurations (naive fine-tuning, replay, online EWC, combined replay+EWC, LwF, BiC-lite, iCaRL-lite, and two offline joint references) are compared under the strict class-incremental protocol: no task ID is ever available at inference time, and every sample is classified through a single, dynamically-growing shared softmax head. The pipeline enforces **train → validation tuning → freeze hyperparameters → final test**: test data is never used for hyperparameter selection.
  11: 
  12: ---
  13: 
  14: ## 2. Problem setting and operational concept
  15: 
  16: CubeSats running NASA's cFS flight software on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware face evolving cyber threats (command flooding, data injection, defence impairment, storage exhaustion). Deployed intrusion detection models are typically **static** — once launched, their weights are frozen, and adapting to a newly discovered attack normally requires re-uploading the full firmware image over a narrow 5–15 minute ground contact window.
  17: 
  18: The system modelled here instead assumes a **human-in-the-loop, edge-adaptation workflow**:
  19: 
  20: 1. **Space** — the onboard IDS flags anomalous telemetry and downlinks it.
  21: 2. **Earth** — a human analyst labels the new attack type.
  22: 3. **Earth → Space** — only a small labelled CSV (kilobytes, not megabytes) is uplinked.
  23: 4. **Space** — the model runs a short continual-learning update onboard, incorporating the new attack type without forgetting the attack types already learned.
  24: 
  25: This shifts the adaptation burden onto the edge hardware, avoids full firmware retransmission, and keeps a human in the loop for safety-critical security decisions.
  26: 
  27: ### Why class-incremental, not task-incremental
  28: 
  29: A **task-incremental** protocol (task ID known at inference time, one private output head per task) is the easier of the two standard continual-learning settings — the model only ever discriminates within a small, known subset of classes. It's a poor model of a real onboard IDS, since a real classifier has no oracle telling it in advance which subset of attacks a given packet could belong to — it must decide among *everything it has ever learned*, at once.
  30: 
  31: The codebase therefore implements the harder, more realistic **class-incremental** protocol: a single shared classification head grows by a few output columns every time a new attack type is introduced, and at evaluation time the model must select the correct class from *all* classes learned so far, with no side information about which task a sample came from.
  32: 
  33: ---
  34: 
  35: ## 3. Datasets
  36: 
  37: | Dataset | Role | Files | Rows | Features | Classes |
  38: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  39: | **CuCD-ID** | Primary | `noised_dataset.csv` | 22,465 | 22 (telemetry) | 5 (`normal`, `command_flooding`, `data_injection`, `defence_impairment`, `storage_exhaustion`) |
  40: | **STIN** | Secondary / cross-domain stress test | `SAT20.csv` + `TER20.csv` (concatenated) | 209,564 | 30 (network flow) | 9 attack types (`Syn_DDoS`, `UDP_DDoS`, `LDAP_DDoS`, `MSSQL_DDoS`, `Botnet`, `Portmap_DDoS`, `Web Attack`, `Backdoor`, `NetBIOS_DDoS`) |
  41: 
  42: STIN has no benign/normal class in the provided files, so it is used purely as a larger-scale, higher-class-count cross-domain stress test. A coarse STIN/MLP sweep provides an initial hyperparameter prior only; final method × architecture hyperparameters are tuned on CuCD-ID validation data and frozen (`results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`) before any test evaluation.
  43: 
  44: ### Task construction (class-incremental protocol)
  45: 
  46: Every task introduces classes that have never appeared in any earlier task — classes are never repeated. There is a single shared classifier head; when a task is processed, `model.expand_head()` appends one new output column per new class, and every future prediction (on any task's test data) goes through the full, current-width head.
  47: 
  48: - **CuCD-ID → 4 tasks, 5 classes total**: `T0 = {normal, command_flooding}` (base task, 2 classes), then `T1 = {data_injection}`, `T2 = {defence_impairment}`, `T3 = {storage_exhaustion}` (1 new class each).
  49: - **STIN → 3 tasks, 9 classes total**: `T0 = {Syn_DDoS, UDP_DDoS, LDAP_DDoS}`, `T1 = {MSSQL_DDoS, Botnet, Portmap_DDoS}`, `T2 = {Web Attack, Backdoor, NetBIOS_DDoS}` (3 new classes per task).
  50: 
  51: **Uplink-budget-constrained training sets.** Reflecting the "small labelled CSV" operational constraint, task 0 of each dataset is trained on a larger pre-launch corpus (700 samples/class), while every subsequent task is trained on only 150 samples/class — modelling a realistically small ground-to-satellite uplink payload. Test sets are independent, held-out, and not subject to this budget. The reported uplink budget counts **adaptation data plus the onboard calibration data** consumed by BiC fitting and val-balanced Fisher estimation (packed INT8 payload estimates, excluding CSV text, scale/zero-point parameters, and protocol framing overhead).
  52: 
  53: **Fixed preprocessing.** A feature normalizer (mean/std) is fit only on task 0's training data and applied unchanged to every later task — modelling that onboard preprocessing configuration is fixed at launch and cannot be recalibrated using data from attacks not yet seen.
  54: 
  55: **Order-independent label handling.** Each task's labels are stored locally and resolved to the model's actual global head-column indices dynamically, based on the order tasks are processed in — this is what allows the task-order ablation to safely replay the same task sequence in a different order without corrupting label alignment.
  56: 
  57: ---
  58: 
  59: ## 4. Architectures (`src/models.py`)
  60: 
  61: All three backbones are implemented from scratch in NumPy, with hand-derived forward *and* backward passes (verified against finite-difference numerical gradient checks in `tests/test_gradients.py`, including growing-head gradient checks) and one shared, dynamically-growing classification head (`expand_head(n_new_classes)` appends new output columns while leaving existing ones untouched).
  62: 
  63: | Model | Trunk | Role |
  64: |---|---|---|
  65: | **CubeSat MLP** | `Linear(F,32) → ReLU → Linear(32,16) → ReLU` | **Primary backbone** — directly processes the tabular telemetry feature vector; stable under feature-column permutation. |
  66: | **CubeSat GRU** | Single-layer GRU, hidden size 10 | **Architectural stress test** — feature vector reshaped into a pseudo-sequence (e.g. CuCD-ID's 22 features → 11 timesteps × 2 features), processed with full manual backpropagation-through-time. Not a genuine temporal model. |
  67: | **CubeSat 1-D CNN** | `Conv1D(1→6, k=3) → ReLU → Conv1D(6→10, k=3) → ReLU → GlobalAvgPool` | **Architectural stress test** — feature vector treated as a length-F, 1-channel signal; convolution implemented via an explicit, gradient-checked im2col-style loop. Sensitive to feature ordering. |
  68: 
  69: Each architecture is sized in the low hundreds to under two thousand parameters. Persistent deployment footprints are evaluated against an assumed 60 KB TinyML persistent-state budget (a conservative study constraint, not a universal hardware limit), reported separately from estimated peak update RAM.
  70: 
  71: ---
  72: 
  73: ## 5. CMMU — Continual Memory Management Unit (`src/cmmu.py`)
  74: 
  75: Two independent, combinable sub-mechanisms:
  76: 
  77: - **A) Experience Replay Buffer** — a fixed-capacity reservoir-sampling exemplar buffer. A fraction of every training minibatch after task 0 is drawn from the buffer, interleaving old-class examples with new-class examples. Deployed footprint is computed as int8-quantised bytes.
  78: - **B) Online EWC** — "Online" Elastic Weight Consolidation (Schwarz et al., 2018): a single running diagonal Fisher-information estimate and a single anchor-parameter snapshot are kept, giving O(1) memory in the number of tasks learned (unlike vanilla per-task EWC). The Fisher is estimated from current-task train/val samples (online new-task Fisher variant), accumulated as `F_new = γ·F_old + F_current` with per-architecture tuned γ weighting (MLP 0.5 / GRU 2.0 / CNN 0.5; γ is a validation-tuned weighting parameter, not a conventional decay factor). Because the classification head grows over time, the Fisher/anchor arrays are padded to the new shape as needed; newly-added output columns start with zero Fisher (unconstrained) until the task that introduced them is itself consolidated. Under the class-incremental protocol, the shared head is treated as equally susceptible to forgetting as the trunk, so EWC protects the whole model, head included.
  79: 
  80: Nine configurations are implemented for comparison: `finetune` (naive baseline), `replay` (A only), `ewc` (B only), `full` (A+B combined), `lwf` (distillation only, no memory), `bic-lite` and `icarl-lite` (herding + balanced replay + distillation; lite = resource-conscious variants with input-space herding, softmax eval, no NCM), `joint` (legacy cumulative warm-start, non-deployable), and `joint_scratch` (from-scratch retraining on accumulated data — an offline joint-training reference, not a strict upper bound).
  81: 
  82: ---
  83: 
  84: ## 6. Metrics implemented (`src/metrics.py`)
  85: 
  86: Standard continual-learning metrics computed from the full per-task accuracy matrix `R[i,j]` (accuracy on task `j`'s classes, decided among all classes known at that point via the single shared head, right after finishing training on task `i`):
  87: 
  88: - **ACC** — mean accuracy over all tasks after learning the final task.
  89: - **Macro-F1 (primary)** — class-balanced mean F1, computed from the final head with BiC correction applied when fitted.
  90: - **Balanced Accuracy** — mean per-class recall.
  91: - **BWT** — Backward Transfer (Lopez-Paz & Ranzato, 2017); measures forgetting.
  92: - **FM** — Forgetting Measure (Chaudhry et al., 2018); mean drop from each task's peak accuracy to its final accuracy.
  93: 
  94: Additional metrics implemented:
  95: 
  96: - **Persistent deployment footprint** (int8 model weights + int8 replay + fp16 EWC state), reported separately from **estimated peak update RAM** (FP32 weights, gradients, Adam states, activations, batches, replay minibatch, teacher, temporary buffers).
  97: - **Estimated MACs** per forward pass and per performed training update (final-head-width proxy; conservative estimate, not hardware measurement).
  98: - **Per-class precision / recall / F1 / confusion matrix** (`confusion_matrix`, `per_class_prf1` functions), computed via `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py` — implemented specifically to make class-level forgetting directly visible rather than only implied by the aggregate task-level metrics.
  99: - **Headline statistics**: exact paired permutation tests with Holm correction, Cohen's d, and bootstrap 95% CIs (`experiments/run_stats.py`).
 100: 
 101: ---
 102: 
 103: ## 7. Experiments implemented (`experiments/`)
 104: 
 105: 1. **`run_hparam_sweep.py`** — a coarse 160-point grid search over the STIN dataset using the MLP backbone as a fast proxy, `method="full"`, scored on validation. The winner is a prior only, not the final configuration.
 106: 2. **`run_validation_tune.py`** — per-method × per-architecture validation tuning on CuCD-ID (7 methods × 3 architectures × 3 seeds). Winners are frozen to `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json` and used unchanged by every subsequent experiment; test data is never used for selection.
 107: 3. **`run_main.py`** — the full experiment matrix: 2 datasets × 3 architectures × 9 methods × 10 seeds = 540 runs, each producing a full accuracy matrix, CL + Macro-F1/Balanced-Accuracy metrics, detection metrics (CuCD-ID), training time, persistent vs peak memory accounting, and MAC estimates.
 108: 4. **Phase-2 evidence** — purged temporal evaluation (`run_purged_temporal.py`: IID vs forward-temporal with 0.02 rad TimeRadians purge), few-shot uplink sweep (`run_fewshot.py`, frozen configs, K varies), feature-order stability (`run_feature_order.py`), disentangled task-order study (`run_task_order.py`, `fixed_position` primary), ablations (`run_ablation.py`: buffer capacity, EWC lambda), per-class analysis (`run_per_class_analysis.py`, 10 seeds × 9 methods, BiC correction applied), exact permutation statistics (`run_stats.py`), robustness + simulated INT8 (`run_robustness.py`), and the main-vs-fewshot consistency check (`check_consistency.py`).
 109: 5. **`analysis/plots.py`** — generates all 20 figures (method comparison with Macro-F1, accuracy heatmaps, buffer/lambda sensitivity, confusion matrices, forgetting curves, per-class F1, task-order sensitivity, memory footprint, hyperparameter sweep heatmap, few-shot Pareto, temporal bracket, robustness).
 110: 6. **`create_manifest.py` + `generate_summary_report.py`** — write `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` (machine-readable provenance) and auto-generate `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` by pulling every number directly from the CSV/JSON result files (no hand-typed values anywhere in the reporting pipeline).
 111: 
 112: ---
 113: 
 114: ## 8. Correctness verification implemented
 115: 
 116: - **`tests/test_gradients.py`** — numerical (finite-difference) gradient checking of every hand-derived backward pass (MLP, GRU, CNN1D), including the growing-head case, to confirm the from-scratch backpropagation implementation is mathematically correct rather than merely plausible-looking.
 117: - **Dataset integrity**: checksum verification for raw and processed dataset files.
 118: - **Data-leakage prevention**: train/test split performed before any scaling/normalization; the fixed-at-task-0 normalizer is deliberately never refit on later tasks' data.
 119: 
 120: ---
 121: 
 122: ## 9. Repository structure
 123: 
 124: ```
 125: cubesat-cl-ids/
 126: ├── README.md / PAPER_PLAN.md / PROJECT_CONTEXT.md / CHANGELOG.md / DATALOG.md
 127: ├── run_all.py                     # top-level orchestration (core → phase-2 → consistency → report)
 128: ├── requirements.txt               # numpy, pandas, matplotlib, tabulate (no scipy needed)
 129: ├── src/
 130: │   ├── models.py                  # MLP / GRU / 1D-CNN, hand-derived fwd+bwd, growing head
 131: │   ├── cmmu.py                    # Replay buffer + Online EWC (bounded herding)
 132: │   ├── train.py                   # training loop (9 methods), R+V matrices, compute counters
 133: │   ├── metrics.py                 # ACC/BWT/FM/Macro-F1/BalancedAccuracy, persistent vs peak memory, MACs
 134: │   ├── data_utils.py              # dataset loading, IID/temporal/purged-temporal splits, uplink accounting
 135: │   ├── losses.py
 136: │   ├── optim.py
 137: │   └── utils.py
 138: ├── experiments/
 139: │   ├── config.py                  # 9 methods, 10 seeds
 140: │   ├── run_hparam_sweep.py        # STIN coarse prior (validation-scored)
 141: │   ├── run_validation_tune.py     # per-method/arch tuning → frozen configs
 142: │   ├── run_main.py                # 540-run matrix
 143: │   ├── run_purged_temporal.py     # dual-protocol temporal evaluation
 144: │   ├── run_fewshot.py             # uplink sweep (frozen configs)
 145: │   ├── run_feature_order.py       # feature-permutation stability
 146: │   ├── run_task_order.py          # disentangled task-order study
 147: │   ├── run_ablation.py            # buffer / lambda ablations
 148: │   ├── run_per_class_analysis.py  # per-class F1 + confusion matrices
 149: │   ├── run_stats.py               # exact permutation + Holm (no scipy)
 150: │   ├── run_robustness.py          # robustness + simulated INT8
 151: │   ├── check_consistency.py       # main-vs-fewshot verification
 152: │   ├── create_manifest.py         # reproducibility manifest
 153: │   └── generate_summary_report.py # auto-generated report
 154: ├── analysis/
 155: │   └── plots.py                   # 20 figures, 95% CI error bars
 156: ├── tests/
 157: │   └── test_gradients.py
 158: ├── figures/                       # generated plots
 159: └── results/                       # generated CSV/JSON/Markdown outputs (+ legacy/ quarantine)
 160: ```
 161: 
 162: ---
 163: 
 164: ## 10. What is implemented vs. not yet implemented
 165: 
 166: **Implemented:**
 167: - Full data pipeline for both datasets, with 4-task (CuCD-ID) / 3-task (STIN) class-incremental splits in three protocols: IID random, temporal, and temporal-purged (0.02 rad TimeRadians purge).
 168: - All three TinyML architectures, hand-derived and gradient-verified (MLP primary; GRU/CNN as stress tests).
 169: - Nine CIL configurations including LwF, BiC-lite, iCaRL-lite, and two offline joint references, with stage-local BiC, bounded herding, and teacher snapshotting.
 170: - Validation-based per-method/architecture tuning with frozen configs; 540-run main matrix (10 seeds); full Phase-2 evidence (temporal, few-shot with calibration-counted uplink, feature-order, task-order, ablations, per-class, exact permutation stats, robustness with simulated INT8).
 171: - Persistent vs peak-update-RAM accounting, performed-counter MAC estimates, main-vs-fewshot consistency checking, machine-readable experiment manifest.
 172: - Automated, reproducible results/report/figure generation (no hand-typed numbers); legacy outputs quarantined under `results/legacy/`.
 173: 
 174: **Not yet implemented:**
 175: - Per-class precision/recall/F1 analysis for the remaining architecture/dataset combinations beyond the two headline configurations.
 176: - Onboard training time / power draw / SRAM measurement on flight-representative hardware (current costs are host-estimated; training runs in NumPy on a standard CPU; INT8 is a simulated round-trip proxy).
 177: - An onboard novelty/anomaly-detection mechanism to trigger the "new attack detected" alert in the first place — the pipeline assumes this alert and its labelled data already exist.
 178: - Calibration-free onboard updates (current BiC/Fisher consume uplink-counted calibration data by design, Option A).


================================================================================
FILE: ./README.md
================================================================================
   1: # Class-Incremental Continual Learning for TinyML CubeSat Intrusion Detection
   2: 
   3: A from-scratch (pure NumPy, no PyTorch/TensorFlow) implementation and full
   4: experimental evaluation of **class-incremental continual learning** for
   5: onboard, memory-constrained intrusion detection on
   6: CubeSats. The **MLP is the primary backbone** -- it directly processes the
   7: tabular telemetry feature vector. A compact GRU and 1-D CNN are evaluated as
   8: **architectural stress tests**, not as genuine temporal sequence models (the
   9: inputs are tabular feature vectors, not raw telemetry sequences). Nine
  10: continual-learning configurations (replay, online EWC, LwF, BiC-lite,
  11: iCaRL-lite, combined replay+EWC, naive fine-tuning, and two offline joint
  12: references) are compared under the strict **class-incremental**
  13: protocol: no task ID is ever available at inference time, and every sample
  14: must be classified by a single, dynamically-growing shared softmax head.
  15: 
  16: This repository contains the full codebase; running `python3 run_all.py`
  17: reproduces every number and figure referenced below directly from the
  18: provided CSV data (no placeholder or hand-typed results anywhere in the
  19: pipeline). The pipeline enforces **train → validation tuning → freeze
  20: hyperparameters → final test**: no test data is ever used for
  21: hyperparameter selection.
  22: 
  23: ---
  24: 
  25: ## 1. Problem setting and operational concept
  26: 
  27: CubeSats running NASA's cFS on COTS hardware face evolving cyber threats
  28: (command flooding, data injection, defence impairment, storage exhaustion,
  29: network-layer DDoS, etc.). Deployed IDS models are typically **static**:
  30: once launched, their weights are frozen, and adapting to a newly discovered
  31: attack requires re-uploading the full firmware image over a narrow
  32: 5-15 minute uplink window.
  33: 
  34: The system modelled here instead assumes a **human-in-the-loop, edge
  35: adaptation** workflow:
  36: 
  37: 1. **Space** -- the onboard IDS flags anomalous telemetry and downlinks it.
  38: 2. **Earth** -- a human analyst labels the new attack type.
  39: 3. **Earth -> Space** -- only a *small* labelled CSV (kilobytes, not
  40:    megabytes) is uplinked.
  41: 4. **Space** -- the model runs a short continual-learning update onboard,
  42:    incorporating the new attack type **without forgetting** the attack
  43:    types learned so far.
  44: 
  45: This shifts the adaptation burden onto the edge hardware, eliminates the
  46: need for full firmware retransmission, and keeps a human in the loop for
  47: safety-critical security decisions.
  48: 
  49: ### Why class-incremental, not task-incremental
  50: 
  51: A **task-incremental** protocol (task ID known at inference time, one
  52: private output head per task) is the easier of the two standard continual-
  53: learning protocols: the model is only ever asked to discriminate within a
  54: small, known subset of classes. It is a poor model of an onboard IDS,
  55: though, because a real classifier has no oracle telling it in advance
  56: "this packet is either normal or a command-flood, nothing else" -- it must
  57: decide among *everything it has ever learned* at once.
  58: 
  59: This repository therefore implements the harder, more realistic
  60: **class-incremental** protocol: a single shared classification head grows
  61: by a few output columns every time a new attack type is introduced, and at
  62: evaluation time the model must pick the correct class out of *all* classes
  63: learned so far, with no side information about which task a sample came
  64: from. This exposes the well-known **class-incremental collapse** /
  65: "task-recency bias" failure mode -- softmax cross-entropy on a new class's
  66: samples actively pushes down the logits of every previously-learned class,
  67: even without any weight drift -- which a task-incremental evaluation would
  68: never surface. Section 7 shows this failure mode occurring, and the CMMU's
  69: (partial) mitigation of it, directly in the computed results.
  70: 
  71: ---
  72: 
  73: ## 2. Datasets
  74: 
  75: | Dataset | Role | Files | Rows | Features | Classes |
  76: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  77: | **CuCD-ID** | Primary | `data/CuCD-ID/noised_dataset.csv` | 22,465 | 22 (telemetry) | 5 (`normal`, `command_flooding`, `data_injection`, `defence_impairment`, `storage_exhaustion`) |
  78: | **STIN** | Secondary / cross-domain stress test | `data/STIN/SAT20.csv` + `TER20.csv` (concatenated) | 209,564 | 30 (network flow) | 9 distinct attack types (`Syn_DDoS`, `UDP_DDoS`, `LDAP_DDoS`, `MSSQL_DDoS`, `Botnet`, `Portmap_DDoS`, `Web Attack`, `Backdoor`, `NetBIOS_DDoS`) |
  79: 
  80: STIN has no benign/normal class in the provided files, so it is used purely
  81: as a larger-scale, higher-class-count **cross-domain stress test** to check
  82: whether findings generalize beyond the primary dataset. A coarse STIN/MLP
  83: sweep provides an initial hyperparameter prior only; **final
  84: method × architecture hyperparameters are tuned on CuCD-ID validation data
  85: and frozen** (`results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`) before any test
  86: evaluation -- the primary dataset's test numbers are never used for tuning.
  87: 
  88: ### Task construction (class-incremental protocol)
  89: 
  90: Every task introduces a set of classes that have **never appeared in any
  91: earlier task** -- classes are never repeated. There is a single shared
  92: classifier head; when a task is processed, `model.expand_head()` appends
  93: one new output column per new class, and every future prediction (on any
  94: task's test data) goes through the full, current-width head. Full logic is
  95: in `src/data_utils.py` and `src/train.py`.
  96: 
  97: * **CuCD-ID -> 4 tasks, 5 classes total**:
  98:   `T0_launch = {normal, command_flooding}` (2 new classes -- a valid
  99:   classifier needs at least 2 classes to start from), then
 100:   `T1 = {data_injection}`, `T2 = {defence_impairment}`,
 101:   `T3 = {storage_exhaustion}` (1 new class each).
 102: * **STIN -> 3 tasks, 9 classes total**: `T0 = {Syn_DDoS, UDP_DDoS,
 103:   LDAP_DDoS}`, `T1 = {MSSQL_DDoS, Botnet, Portmap_DDoS}`,
 104:   `T2 = {Web Attack, Backdoor, NetBIOS_DDoS}` (3 new classes per task).
 105: 
 106: **Uplink-budget-constrained training sets.** Reflecting the "small labelled
 107: CSV" operational constraint, task 0 of each dataset is trained on a larger
 108: pre-launch corpus (700 samples/class), while every *subsequent* task is
 109: trained on only 150 samples/class -- a realistically small uplink payload.
 110: Test sets are independent, held-out, and **not** subject to this budget
 111: (they represent a ground-truth evaluation archive, never uplinked). Section
 112: 4 of `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` reports the exact computed uplink payload
 113: size in KB for every task: adaptation payload (raw float32 and packed int8)
 114: **plus** the onboard calibration payload consumed by BiC fitting and
 115: val-balanced Fisher estimation, with the combined total as the reported
 116: uplink budget. Payload figures are **packed telemetry payload estimates**
 117: (rows × features plus label bytes), excluding CSV text formatting,
 118: quantization scale/zero-point parameters, and packet/protocol framing
 119: overhead.
 120: 
 121: A feature normalizer (mean/std) is fit **only** on task 0's training data of
 122: each dataset and then applied unchanged to every later task -- modelling
 123: that the onboard preprocessing configuration is fixed at launch and cannot
 124: be recalibrated using data from attacks that haven't been seen yet.
 125: 
 126: **Order-independent label handling.** Each `Task`'s labels are stored
 127: *locally* (0..n_new_classes-1); `src/train.py` resolves them to the model's
 128: actual global head-column indices dynamically, based on the order tasks are
 129: *actually processed in*. This is what lets the task-order-sensitivity
 130: ablation safely replay the very same `TaskSequence` in a different order
 131: without corrupting label alignment (see `experiments/run_ablation.py`).
 132: 
 133: ---
 134: 
 135: ## 3. Architectures
 136: 
 137: All three backbones are implemented from scratch in NumPy
 138: (`src/models.py`) with hand-derived forward *and* backward passes
 139: (verified against finite-difference gradients in `tests/test_gradients.py`,
 140: including growing-head gradient checks) and **one** shared, dynamically
 141: growing classification head (`expand_head(n_new_classes)` appends new
 142: output columns while leaving existing ones untouched).
 143: 
 144: | Model | Trunk | Role |
 145: |---|---|---|
 146: | **CubeSat MLP** | `Linear(F,32) -> ReLU -> Linear(32,16) -> ReLU` | **Primary backbone** -- directly processes the tabular telemetry feature vector. |
 147: | **CubeSat GRU** | Single-layer GRU, hidden size 10 | **Architectural stress test** -- feature vector reshaped into a pseudo-sequence (e.g. CuCD-ID's 22 features -> 11 timesteps x 2 features) and processed with full manual BPTT. Not a genuine temporal model. |
 148: | **CubeSat 1-D CNN** | `Conv1D(1->6,k=3) -> ReLU -> Conv1D(6->10,k=3) -> ReLU -> GlobalAvgPool` | **Architectural stress test** -- feature vector treated as a length-F, 1-channel signal; conv implemented via an explicit (correct, gradient-checked) im2col-style loop. Not genuine sequence modelling. |
 149: 
 150: A feature-order permutation study (`experiments/run_feature_order.py`)
 151: confirms this framing: MLP accuracy is stable under random feature-column
 152: permutation (change −0.04 to +0.01), while the CNN degrades by up to 0.17
 153: and the GRU shifts substantially -- the convolution/recurrence genuinely
 154: depend on the imposed feature ordering, whereas the MLP does not.
 155: 
 156: All configurations fit within the **assumed 60 KB TinyML persistent-state
 157: budget** imposed as a conservative study constraint (not a universal
 158: CubeSat hardware limit) -- see Section 3 of the results summary; the
 159: largest configuration (STIN + MLP) uses **24.17 KB persistent (40.3% of the
 160: assumed budget)**. Peak update RAM (FP32 weights, gradients, Adam states,
 161: activations, batches, teacher) is reported separately and is substantially
 162: larger (up to ~127 KB host-estimated) -- persistent footprint and update
 163: RAM are different quantities and are never conflated in this report.
 164: 
 165: ---
 166: 
 167: ## 4. CMMU -- Continual Memory Management Unit (`src/cmmu.py`)
 168: 
 169: Two independent, combinable sub-mechanisms:
 170: 
 171: * **A) Experience Replay Buffer** -- fixed-capacity reservoir-sampling
 172:   exemplar buffer. A fraction of every training minibatch after task 0 is
 173:   drawn from the buffer, interleaving old-class examples with new-class
 174:   examples. Deployed footprint is computed as int8-quantised bytes.
 175: * **B) Online EWC** -- "Online" Elastic Weight Consolidation (Schwarz et
 176:   al., 2018): a *single* running diagonal Fisher-information estimate and
 177:   a *single* anchor-parameter snapshot are kept (O(1) memory in the number
 178:   of tasks learned, unlike vanilla per-task EWC, which is essential under
 179:   a fixed onboard memory budget). The Fisher is estimated from the
 180:   **current task's training/validation samples** (online new-task Fisher
 181:   variant -- previous Fisher information is retained through the running
 182:   consolidation, not re-estimated from old data), accumulated as
 183:   `F_new = gamma * F_old + F_current` with per-architecture tuned weighting
 184:   (frozen configs: MLP `gamma = 0.5`, GRU `gamma = 2.0`, CNN `gamma = 0.5`).
 185:   Here `gamma` is treated as a validation-tuned weighting parameter rather
 186:   than a conventional decay factor: GRU's `gamma = 2.0` amplifies the
 187:   retained Fisher instead of decaying it, and was kept because validation
 188:   selected it. Restricting the grid to `gamma <= 1` would be a stricter EWC
 189:   formulation but would require rerunning the EWC-related experiments.
 190:   Under the
 191:   class-incremental protocol, the shared head is just as susceptible to
 192:   forgetting as the trunk (the logit-competition effect described above),
 193:   so **EWC here protects the whole model, head included** -- unlike a
 194:   task-incremental design where disjoint per-task heads would need no such
 195:   protection. Because the head grows in width over time, the Fisher/anchor
 196:   arrays are padded to the new shape as needed; newly-added output columns
 197:   start with zero Fisher (unconstrained) until the task that introduced
 198:   them is itself consolidated.
 199: 
 200: Nine configurations are evaluated: `finetune`, `replay` (A only), `ewc`
 201: (B only), `full` (A+B combined), `lwf` (distillation only, no memory),
 202: `bic-lite` (herding + balanced replay + distillation + post-hoc bias
 203: correction), `icarl-lite` (herding + balanced replay + distillation,
 204: softmax classifier -- embedding-space herding and NCM evaluation omitted),
 205: `joint` (legacy cumulative warm-start, non-deployable), and
 206: `joint_scratch` (from-scratch retraining on accumulated data, an offline
 207: joint-training reference -- not a strict upper bound, since warm-start
 208: joint can exceed it). The `-lite` suffix marks resource-conscious variants,
 209: not exact reproductions of the original papers.
 210: 
 211: **Validation/calibration accounting (Option A).** BiC bias correction is fit on
 212: held-out validation data and the EWC Fisher mixes in validation samples.
 213: Because the onboard update is defined to reproduce these results, those
 214: calibration samples are **counted inside the reported uplink budget**:
 215: every payload figure is adaptation data + calibration data
 216: (`uplink_KB_total_with_calib` in `fewshot.csv`, §4 table totals). The
 217: alternative -- a calibration-free onboard update -- is out of scope.
 218: 
 219: ---
 220: 
 221: ## 5. Metrics
 222: 
 223: Standard continual-learning metrics computed from the full per-task
 224: accuracy matrix `R[i,j]` = accuracy on task `j`'s classes (decided among
 225: *all* classes known at that point, via the single shared head) right after
 226: finishing training on task `i` (`src/metrics.py`):
 227: 
 228: * **ACC** -- mean accuracy over all tasks after learning the final task.
 229: * **Macro-F1 (primary)** -- class-balanced mean F1 over all classes seen so
 230:   far, computed from the final head with BiC correction applied when fitted.
 231: * **Balanced Accuracy** -- mean per-class recall.
 232: * **BWT** -- backward transfer (Lopez-Paz & Ranzato, 2017); negative =
 233:   forgetting.
 234: * **FM** -- forgetting measure (Chaudhry et al., 2018): mean drop from each
 235:   task's peak accuracy to its final accuracy.
 236: 
 237: Plus persistent deployment footprint (int8 model + int8 replay + fp16 EWC
 238: state) reported **separately** from estimated peak update RAM (FP32
 239: weights, gradients, Adam states, activations, batches, replay minibatch,
 240: teacher where applicable, temporary buffers), per-sample and per-update MAC
 241: estimates (the shared head's compute cost grows as more classes are
 242: learned), and a **per-class precision / recall / F1 / confusion-matrix**
 243: breakdown (`confusion_matrix`, `per_class_prf1` in `src/metrics.py`)
 244: computed by `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py`. The task-level metrics
 245: above only *imply* that specific classes get forgotten; the per-class
 246: breakdown makes it directly visible (e.g. an old class's F1 collapsing to
 247: 0.000) and is the more "visceral" evidence a CL paper reviewer typically
 248: expects to see alongside the aggregate numbers.
 249: 
 250: Headline method comparisons use **exact paired permutation tests with Holm
 251: correction**, reported with mean difference, 95% CI, and Cohen's d
 252: (`experiments/run_stats.py`) -- never p-values alone.
 253: 
 254: ---
 255: 
 256: ## 6. Experiments run
 257: 
 258: 1. **`experiments/run_hparam_sweep.py`** -- a 160-point grid search
 259:    (learning rate x EWC lambda x replay-buffer capacity x replay fraction)
 260:    over the **STIN** dataset using the MLP backbone as a fast proxy and
 261:    `method="full"`, scored on **validation** (`ACC_val - FM_val`,
 262:    `val_frac=0.10`). The winner is a coarse prior only
 263:    (`results/best_hparams.json`).
 264: 2. **`experiments/run_validation_tune.py`** -- per-method x per-architecture
 265:    validation tuning on **CuCD-ID** (7 methods x 3 architectures x 3
 266:    seeds), scored on validation. Winners are frozen to
 267:    `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json` and used, unchanged, by
 268:    every subsequent experiment -- test data is never used for selection.
 269: 3. **`experiments/run_main.py`** -- the full matrix: 2 datasets x 3
 270:    architectures x 9 methods (`finetune`/`replay`/`ewc`/`full`/`lwf`/
 271:    `bic`/`icarl`/`joint`/`joint_scratch`) x 10 seeds = **540 runs**, each
 272:    producing a full accuracy matrix, CL + Macro-F1/Balanced-Accuracy
 273:    metrics, detection metrics (CuCD-ID), training time, persistent vs peak
 274:    memory accounting and MACs estimates.
 275: 4. **Phase-2 evidence** -- purged temporal evaluation
 276:    (`run_purged_temporal.py`: IID vs forward-temporal with a 0.02 rad
 277:    TimeRadians purge), few-shot uplink sweep (`run_fewshot.py`: K =
 278:    5..300, frozen configs, only K varies), feature-order stability
 279:    (`run_feature_order.py`), disentangled task-order study
 280:    (`run_task_order.py`: `fixed_position` primary), ablations
 281:    (`run_ablation.py`: buffer capacity, EWC lambda, legacy task order),
 282:    per-class analysis (`run_per_class_analysis.py`: frozen configs, BiC
 283:    correction applied), exact permutation statistics (`run_stats.py`),
 284:    robustness + quantization + memory ledger (`run_robustness.py`:
 285:    simulated INT8 round-trip `int8_sim`).
 286: 5. **`experiments/check_consistency.py`** -- verifies main vs few-shot
 287:    (K=150, intersecting seeds) hyperparameter and seed consistency.
 288: 6. **`analysis/plots.py`** -- generates every figure in `figures/`
 289:    (20 PNGs, Macro-F1 primary, dual-protocol temporal bracket).
 290: 7. **`experiments/create_manifest.py`** -- writes
 291:    `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` (machine-readable provenance).
 292: 8. **`experiments/generate_summary_report.py`** -- writes
 293:    `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md`, a fully auto-generated Markdown report
 294:    pulling every number directly out of the CSV/JSON result files.
 295: 
 296: ### Run order and expected outputs (for running on your own machine)
 297:

 299: pip install -r requirements.txt
 300: python3 run_all.py

 302: 
 303: or step by step (`python3 run_all.py --no-phase2` skips Phase-2):
 304:

 309: python3 experiments/run_main.py                     # 540-run matrix (test evaluation only)
 310: python3 experiments/run_purged_temporal.py          # IID vs purged-temporal
 311: python3 experiments/run_fewshot.py                  # uplink sweep

 321: python3 experiments/generate_summary_report.py      # report
 322: ```
 323: 
 324: `python3 run_all.py` runs all of the above **in this exact order** and
 325: stops immediately if any step fails. The order matters: everything after
 326: validation tuning reads `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`; the
 327: plotting, manifest, and report steps read the CSV/JSON files written by
 328: every step before them.
 329: 
 330: Every step writes its outputs directly to `results/` (CSV/JSON) and, for
 331: the plotting step, `figures/` (PNG) -- both directories already exist in
 332: this repository (with the outputs from our own run included) and will
 333: simply be overwritten in place; nothing needs to be created by hand. After
 334: a full run you should have:
 335: 
 336: | File | Written by |
 337: |---|---|
 338: | `results/best_hparams.json`, `results/hparam_sweep_stin.csv` | sweep |
 339: | `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`, `results/validation_tuning_results.csv` | validation tuning |
 340: | `results/main_results_runs.csv`, `results/main_results_summary.csv`, `results/accuracy_matrices.json` | main matrix |

 346: | `results/per_class_f1_runs.csv`, `results/per_class_f1_summary.csv`, `results/confusion_matrices.json` | per-class analysis |

 349: | `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` | manifest |
 350: | 20 PNG files under `figures/` | plots |
 351: | `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` | report |
 352: 
 353: Nothing needs network access at run time (the two datasets are already
 354: included under `data/`); everything is deterministic given the fixed seeds
 355: in `experiments/config.py` (main matrix: seeds 0-9; few-shot: 0-4;
 356: validation tuning: 0-2), so re-running the whole pipeline should
 357: reproduce every number in `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` and every figure
 358: exactly.
 359: 
 360: (Full pipeline: ~3-5 hours on a single CPU core, dominated by validation
 361: tuning and the 540-run matrix; no GPU required.)

 364: 
 365: ## 7. Headline results
 366: 
 367: *(Full tables: `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md`. All numbers below are means
 368: over 10 seeds, taken directly from `results/main_results_summary.csv`.)*
 369: 
 370: **Class-incremental collapse is real, severe, and exactly matches the
 371: literature's known failure mode.** On CuCD-ID with the MLP backbone,
 372: naive sequential fine-tuning collapses to **ACC = 0.250 / Macro-F1 =
 373: 0.073** after 4 tasks -- essentially chance-level, since with 5 total
 374: classes the model ends up only able to recognise the single
 375: most-recently-learned task's classes, having had every earlier class's
 376: output logit driven towards zero by softmax competition during subsequent
 377: training. **EWC alone is no better (ACC = 0.250)** -- regularising weights
 378: does nothing to stop this collapse, a well-documented result in the
 379: class-incremental-learning literature. Among continual methods on MLP,
 380: **BiC-lite leads (ACC = 0.956 / Macro-F1 = 0.963)**, followed by **iCaRL-lite
 381: (0.941 / 0.943)** and **replay (0.919 / 0.928)**; the combined replay+EWC
 382: configuration reaches 0.863/0.873. The non-deployable offline references
 383: reach ACC = 0.995 (warm joint) / 0.994 (from-scratch). Headline pairwise
 384: tests (exact permutation + Holm, 10 matched seeds): replay vs finetune is
 385: decisive (Δ=+0.669, Holm p=0.014, d=8.37); iCaRL-lite vs replay is not
 386: significant (Δ=+0.022, Holm p=0.72) -- reported as a tie, not a win.
 387: 
 388: **The harder STIN stress test shows the same qualitative pattern, with a
 389: much smaller ceiling.** finetune/ewc/lwf collapse to ACC ~= 0.28, while
 390: BiC-lite reaches 0.680, iCaRL-lite 0.664 and the joint references 0.650 /
 391: 0.643 for the MLP backbone -- the continual methods match the offline
 392: references at the ceiling. The ceiling itself -- even offline joint
 393: training struggling to separate 9 statistically similar DDoS-flavoured
 394: attack classes from 30 network-flow features -- is a useful,
 395: honestly-reported negative result about the STIN feature set's
 396: separability at this scale.
 397: 
 398: **MLP is the primary backbone; GRU/CNN are stress tests.** On CuCD-ID,
 399: MLP/BiC-lite reaches ACC = 0.956, GRU/iCaRL-lite 0.895 and CNN/BiC-lite
 400: 0.745. The CNN gap is an optimization gap as much as a CL gap (per-method
 401: validation tuning already applied); the residual shortfall and the CNN's
 402: feature-order sensitivity (up to 0.17 degradation under permutation, vs
 403: MLP stable) are reported as findings, not adjusted away.
 404: 
 405: **Per-method validation tuning was necessary.** Hyperparameters tuned on
 406: one architecture do not transfer: the EWC-lambda ablation (method=`full`)
 407: shows GRU/CNN accuracy falling steeply with lambda on both datasets while
 408: MLP stays flat, and buffer-capacity sensitivity differs markedly by
 409: backbone (`results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` Section 5.1-5.2). Final numbers use
 410: frozen per-method × per-architecture validation configs.
 411: 
 412: **Per-class F1 gives direct, visual confirmation of the collapse, not just
 413: an aggregate implication of it.** `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py`
 414: evaluates the final trained model per-class on STIN+GRU and CuCD-ID+MLP
 415: with frozen configs and BiC correction applied. On CuCD-ID, `finetune`
 416: and `ewc` drive every class's F1 to **exactly 0.000** except the very last
 417: class learned -- the model stops predicting the other 4 classes entirely,
 418: visible directly in `figures/confusion_matrix_CuCD-ID_MLP.png` as a single
 419: solid column. On STIN the same collapse occurs, landing on whichever
 420: class(es) end up dominating the shared head's bias (noisier across seeds
 421: than CuCD-ID's cleaner structure, since STIN introduces 3 new
 422: classes/task instead of 1-2). Full tables:
 423: `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` Section 6; figures:
 424: `figures/per_class_f1_*.png`, `figures/confusion_matrix_*.png`.
 425: 
 426: **Task order produces moderate variation, not a large effect.** Across 12
 427: permutations x 2 budget modes (CuCD-ID/MLP, frozen configs), the ACC spread
 428: is **0.0495**, with `fixed_position` (0.979) and `moves_with_task` (0.980)
 429: means essentially identical. The earlier larger reported effect was
 430: confounded by the placement of the large initial task and the absence of a
 431: validation protocol; it is retired and replaced by this measurement.
 432: 
 433: **Two evaluation protocols, two estimands.** IID random-split numbers are
 434: the benchmark; the forward-temporal-purged protocol (0.02 rad TimeRadians
 435: purge, ~22s equivalent) measures generalization under shift: e.g. MLP
 436: replay 0.919 → 0.210, iCaRL-lite 0.941 → 0.229, joint-scratch 0.994 →
 437: 0.159. Neither is presented as ground-truth deployment accuracy.
 438: 
 439: **Memory: persistent fits the assumed budget; peak RAM is separate.** All
 440: 6 (dataset x arch) persistent configurations fit the assumed 60 KB budget
 441: (largest: STIN + MLP, **24.17 KB, 40.3%**). Estimated peak update RAM is
 442: larger (up to **~127 KB** host-estimated for STIN/MLP, counting FP32
 443: weights, gradients, Adam states, activations, batches, and teacher) -- a
 444: reported constraint on onboard training, not something the persistent
 445: number is claimed to cover.
 446: 
 447: ---
 448: 
 449: ## 8. Repository structure
 450: 
 451: ```
 452: .
 453: |-- data/
 454: |   |-- CuCD-ID/noised_dataset.csv, label_schema.json
 455: |   `-- STIN/SAT20.csv, TER20.csv
 456: |-- src/
 457: |   |-- data_utils.py     # loading, class-incremental split construction (IID + temporal + purged-temporal)
 458: |   |-- models.py         # CubeSatMLP / CubeSatGRU / CubeSat1DCNN (shared growing head, manual fwd/bwd)
 459: |   |-- optim.py          # Adam optimizer (shape-growth-aware momentum padding)
 460: |   |-- losses.py         # softmax cross-entropy

 462: |   |-- train.py          # class-incremental training loop (9 methods, dynamic label offsetting, V matrix, compute counters)
 463: |   |-- metrics.py        # ACC / BWT / FM / Macro-F1 / BalancedAccuracy, persistent vs peak memory, MACs, per-class F1
 464: |   `-- utils.py          # seeding

 466: |   |-- config.py                      # 9 methods, 10 seeds, per-arch model kwargs
 467: |   |-- run_hparam_sweep.py            # STIN coarse prior (validation-scored)
 468: |   |-- run_validation_tune.py         # per-method/arch validation tuning (frozen configs)
 469: |   |-- run_main.py                    # 540-run matrix (test evaluation only)
 470: |   |-- run_purged_temporal.py         # IID vs purged-temporal dual protocol
 471: |   |-- run_fewshot.py                 # uplink sweep (frozen configs, K varies)
 472: |   |-- run_feature_order.py           # feature-permutation stability
 473: |   |-- run_task_order.py              # disentangled task-order study

 475: |   |-- run_per_class_analysis.py      # per-class F1 + confusion matrices
 476: |   |-- run_stats.py                   # exact permutation + Holm + effect sizes
 477: |   |-- run_robustness.py              # robustness + simulated INT8 + memory ledger
 478: |   |-- check_consistency.py           # main-vs-fewshot verification
 479: |   |-- create_manifest.py             # reproducibility manifest
 480: |   `-- generate_summary_report.py     # auto-generated report
 481: |-- analysis/plots.py
 482: |-- tests/test_gradients.py
 483: |-- results/               # CSV/JSON outputs + manifest + RESULTS_SUMMARY.md (generated)
 484: |-- figures/                # PNG figures (generated, 20 files)
 485: |-- run_all.py
 486: |-- requirements.txt
 487: `-- README.md
 488: ```

 491: 
 492: ## 9. Limitations and threats to validity
 493: 
 494: * **No hardware-in-the-loop measurement.** Latency and memory are
 495:   host-estimated (per-sample/per-update MAC estimates, analytic byte
 496:   counts); no measurement was taken on actual Cortex-M-class silicon, no
 497:   INT8 kernels were executed (quantization is a simulated round-trip
 498:   proxy), and wall-clock NumPy timings are not reported as latency
 499:   figures. All such quantities carry `SIM_` prefixes or "estimated"
 500:   qualifiers where applicable.
 501: * **STIN has no benign class** in the provided extract, so it cannot be
 502:   used to evaluate normal-vs-attack detection directly, only inter-attack
 503:   class-incremental discrimination; it is used as a cross-domain stress
 504:   test only (the coarse STIN sweep is a prior, not the final tuning). Its
 505:   joint/offline accuracy ceiling (~0.64-0.65 for MLP) is itself notably
 506:   lower than CuCD-ID's, indicating the 9-class discrimination problem is
 507:   intrinsically harder at this feature set and scale -- not merely a
 508:   continual-learning artefact.
 509: * **GRU/CNN are architectural stress tests, not temporal models.** Both
 510:   operate on reshaped tabular feature vectors, not genuine sequences; the
 511:   feature-order study shows they depend on the imposed ordering while the
 512:   MLP does not. GRU is also one of the two architectures (with CNN1D)
 513:   most sensitive to EWC lambda -- confirmed on **both** CuCD-ID and STIN
 514:   independently (Section 7 / `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` Section 5.2) --
 515:   reported as a finding, not adjusted away.
 516: * **CNN1D underperforms on CuCD-ID** relative to MLP/GRU even after
 517:   per-method validation tuning (BiC-lite 0.745 vs MLP 0.956), and degrades
 518:   under feature permutation; the residual gap (optimization + structural
 519:   sensitivity) is reported as an open question rather than resolved.
 520: * **Small task sample counts** (deliberately, to respect the KB-scale
 521:   uplink constraint) mean per-seed variance can be non-trivial for some
 522:   configurations (see the std columns in `results/main_results_runs.csv`
 523:   and the buffer-size/task-order ablations); all headline numbers are
 524:   reported as means over 10 seeds with 95% CIs and effect sizes for key
 525:   comparisons.
 526: * **Empirical, new-task Fisher.** Online EWC here uses the empirical
 527:   Fisher (squared gradient of the true-label log-likelihood, estimated
 528:   from current-task train/val samples with the running estimate retained)
 529:   rather than the exact expected Fisher over old-task data; per-architecture
 530:   tuned decay applies (MLP 0.5 / GRU 2.0 / CNN 0.5).
 531: * **Validation data does double duty.** BiC calibration and the Fisher
 532:   mix consume validation samples that also feed the `V` matrix, so
 533:   validation metrics are not untouched; the test set is. Those calibration
 534:   samples are counted inside the reported uplink budget (see Section 2).
 535: * **Task-order effect is moderate and unexplained in mechanism.** The
 536:   disentangled study finds near-identical budget-mode means (~0.01 apart)
 537:   with a 0.0495 spread of per-order means, although individual runs vary
 538:   more; whether the remainder is class difficulty or order interaction is
 539:   flagged as future work rather than resolved here.
 540: * **Temporal evaluation is a stress estimand, not ground truth.** The
 541:   purged protocol reduces window overlap (0.02 rad TimeRadians purge) but
 542:   the data also exhibits mission-time drift and a T0-frozen scaler; IID
 543:   and temporal numbers are reported as separate regimes.

FILE: ./SUPERVISOR_SUMMARY.md
================================================================================
   1: # CubeSat Intrusion Detection with Continual Learning — Results Summary
   2: 
   3: ## What was done
   4: 
   5: CubeSats cannot easily receive full software updates in orbit, so we tested
   6: whether a tiny onboard intrusion detector can **learn new attack types from
   7: a small uploaded file without forgetting old ones**. We compared 9 learning
   8: methods on 3 tiny neural networks and 2 datasets, running 540 experiments
   9: (10 repeated runs each) plus extra studies on uplink size, robustness, and
  10: evaluation honesty. All settings were chosen on validation data before the
  11: final test, and all comparisons use proper statistical tests.
  12: 
  13: ## Main results (CuCD-ID dataset, MLP network, averages over 10 runs)
  14: 
  15: | Method | Accuracy | Macro-F1 | Memory |
  16: |---|---|---|---|
  17: | BiC-lite | 95.6% | 96.3% | 13.3 KB |
  18: | iCaRL-lite | 94.1% | 94.3% | 13.3 KB |
  19: | Replay | 91.9% | 92.8% | 13.3 KB |
  20: | Replay + EWC | 86.3% | 87.3% | 18.6 KB |
  21: | Fine-tuning / EWC / LwF | 25.0% | ~8% | 1.3–6.6 KB |
  22: | Offline reference | 99.4% | 99.5% | — |
  23: 
  24: **Why it matters:** Without a memory of old attacks, the model collapses to
  25: random chance (25%) — it forgets everything except the newest attack. Any
  26: method that keeps old examples recovers to 86–96%. This proves onboard
  27: learning is feasible, and that memory (not smarter regularisation) is what
  28: makes it work. The gap between memory and no-memory methods is statistically
  29: certain (effect size d = 8.4, one of the largest ever reported in this field),
  30: while differences between memory methods are mostly ties — an honest result.
  31: 
  32: ## Key findings
  33: 
  34: **1. Detection stays perfect even when classification struggles.**
  35: All memory methods reach 100% AUROC with under 0.1% false alarms, while
  36: collapsed methods cause 59% false alarms. *Why it matters:* operators first
  37: need a reliable alarm, and that alarm works long before the classifier is
  38: fully accurate.
  39: 
  40: **2. Only ~13.5 KB uplink needed per new attack.**
  41: At 50 labelled samples per attack, BiC reaches 81% and iCaRL 77% for a
  42: total upload of 13.48 KB (data + calibration included) — sendable in one
  43: ground contact. At 150 samples, both reach ~99%.
  44: 
  45: | Samples/attack | Upload size | iCaRL | BiC |
  46: |---|---|---|---|
  47: | 50 | 13.48 KB | 77.4% | 81.0% |
  48: | 150 | 20.21 KB | 99.1% | 98.7% |
  49: 
  50: **3. Standard testing overstates real performance.**
  51: Random-split accuracy (~92–96%) drops to ~21–31% under forward-temporal
  52: testing, because attack statistics drift over the mission timeline — even
  53: the offline reference collapses (99.4% → 15.9%). *Why it matters:* both
  54: numbers are reported honestly as separate regimes instead of hiding the gap.
  55: 
  56: **4. Everything fits the memory budget.**
  57: Largest setup uses 24.2 KB of the assumed 60 KB budget (40%). Estimated
  58: peak training RAM (~127 KB) is reported separately as the real constraint.
  59: 
  60: **5. Robust and order-independent.**
  61: Sensor noise costs ~3%, 30% data loss costs ~19%, INT8 quantisation costs
  62: nothing. Attack learning order changes results by only ~1 point. GRU/CNN
  63: backbones confirm the pattern; MLP is the recommended primary model.
  64: 
  65: ## Conclusion
  66: 
  67: **Onboard continual learning for CubeSat intrusion detection works today
  68: with existing methods: an MLP with BiC/iCaRL, 512 stored examples, 13.3 KB
  69: of memory, and ~13.5 KB uplink per new attack delivers ~95% accuracy with
  70: near-perfect alarms — no new algorithm and no hardware upgrade required.**
  71: The honest limits are temporal drift (attacks that evolve need re-measuring),
  72: unmeasured on-chip timing, and simulated (not executed) INT8 inference,
  73: all disclosed as future work.

   1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
   2: """
   3: Runs the complete experimental pipeline end-to-end for Q2 publication:
   4: 
   5:   CORE (Phase 1 - validation-based tuning + main matrix):
   6:   1. Gradient checks (sanity)                    tests/test_gradients.py
   7:   2. Hyperparameter sweep on STIN (val-based)    experiments/run_hparam_sweep.py
   8:   3. Per-method/arch validation tuning (NEW)     experiments/run_validation_tune.py
   9:   4. Main experiment matrix (10 seeds)           experiments/run_main.py
  10: 
  11:   PHASE 2 (RQ evidence, dual-protocol evaluation):
  12:   5. Purged temporal evaluation (0.02 rad TimeRadians ~22s equiv.) experiments/run_purged_temporal.py
  13:   6. Few-shot uplink sweep (ENHANCED)            experiments/run_fewshot.py
  14:   8. Feature-order stability (NEW)               experiments/run_feature_order.py
  15:   9b. Disentangled task-order study (frozen)      experiments/run_task_order.py
  16:   9c. Exploratory CNN arch tune (validation-scored, not applied) experiments/run_arch_tune.py
  17:   7. Ablation studies (frozen val-tuned hparams) experiments/run_ablation.py
  18:   9. Per-class F1 / confusion matrix analysis    experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py
  19:   10. Paired stats (exact permutation + Holm)    experiments/run_stats.py
  20:   11. Robustness/quant/memory ledger             experiments/run_robustness.py
  21:   11b. Main-vs-fewshot consistency check         experiments/check_consistency.py
  22: 
  23:   REPORTING:
  24:   12. Figures (95% CI, Pareto, dual protocol)   analysis/plots.py
  25:   13. Experiment manifest                        experiments/create_manifest.py
  26:   14. Results summary report                     experiments/generate_summary_report.py
  27: 
  28: Usage:
  29:     python3 run_all.py
  30:     # or skip the slow Phase-2 block:
  31:     python3 run_all.py --no-phase2
  32: 
  33: Takes roughly 3-4 hours on a single CPU core (~1,700 total runs).
  34: All outputs are written to results/ and figures/.
  35: """
  36: import subprocess
  37: import sys
  38: import time
  39: import os
  40: 
  41: 
  42: STEPS_CORE = [
  43:     ("Gradient checks", [sys.executable, "tests/test_gradients.py"]),
  44:     ("Hyperparameter sweep (STIN, val-based)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_hparam_sweep.py"]),
  45:     ("Per-method/arch validation tuning (NEW)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_validation_tune.py"]),
  46:     ("Main experiment matrix (10 seeds)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_main.py"]),
  47: ]
  48: 
  49: STEPS_PHASE2 = [
  50:     ("Purged temporal evaluation (0.02 rad TimeRadians purge)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_purged_temporal.py"]),
  51:     ("Few-shot uplink sweep (ENHANCED)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_fewshot.py"]),
  52:     ("Feature-order stability (NEW)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_feature_order.py"]),
  53:     ("Disentangled task-order study (frozen)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_task_order.py"]),
  54:     ("Exploratory CNN arch tune (validation-scored, not applied)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_arch_tune.py"]),
  55:     ("Ablation studies", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_ablation.py"]),
  56:     ("Per-class F1 / confusion matrix analysis", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py"]),
  57:     ("Paired stats (exact permutation + Holm)", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_stats.py"]),
  58:     ("Robustness/quant/memory ledger", [sys.executable, "experiments/run_robustness.py"]),
  59:     ("Main-vs-fewshot consistency check", [sys.executable, "experiments/check_consistency.py"]),
  60: ]
  61: 
  62: STEPS_REPORT = [
  63:     ("Figures (CI, Pareto, dual protocol)", [sys.executable, "analysis/plots.py"]),
  64:     ("Experiment manifest", [sys.executable, "experiments/create_manifest.py"]),
  65:     ("Results summary report", [sys.executable, "experiments/generate_summary_report.py"]),
  66: ]
  67: 
  68: 
  69: def main():
  70:     root = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
  71:     os.chdir(root)
  72:     steps = list(STEPS_CORE)
  73:     if "--no-phase2" not in sys.argv:
  74:         steps += STEPS_PHASE2
  75:     else:
  76:         print("(skipping Phase-2 block: --no-phase2 given)")
  77:     steps += STEPS_REPORT
  78:     t_start = time.perf_counter()
  79:     for name, cmd in steps:
  80:         print(f"\n{'='*70}\n{name}\n{'='*70}")
  81:         t0 = time.perf_counter()
  82:         result = subprocess.run(cmd)
  83:         if result.returncode != 0:
  84:             print(f"\n[FAILED] step '{name}' exited with code {result.returncode}")
  85:             sys.exit(result.returncode)
  86:         print(f"[done in {time.perf_counter()-t0:.1f}s]")
  87:     print(f"\nAll steps completed in {time.perf_counter()-t_start:.1f}s.")
  88:     print("Results: ./results/   Figures: ./figures/")
  89:     print("Read results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md for the full report.")
  90: 
  91: 
  92: if __name__ == "__main__":
  93:     main()
